subject: Business
title: Dollar-Cost Averaging
description: Learn Dollar-Cost Averaging in one minute.

hook.text: You invest $500 monthly regardless of market price. Some months you buy high, some low.

buildup.text: Dollar-cost averaging means investing a fixed amount at regular intervals, ignoring market timing entirely.

discovery.text: When prices drop, your fixed amount buys more shares. When prices rise, it buys fewer. Volatility works for you.

twist.text: Lump-sum investing actually beats DCA two-thirds of the time — but DCA prevents the fear that stops people from investing.

climax.text: The best investment plan is one you actually follow. DCA's simplicity keeps people investing through every market cycle.

punchline.text: Don't time the market. Time in the market wins.

quiz.question: What is the main behavioral advantage of dollar-cost averaging?
options: It removes the fear and hesitation that stops people from investing
It always produces higher returns than lump-sum investing

details.summary: Dollar cost averaging invests a fixed amount at regular intervals regardless of market price. You automatically buy more shares when prices are low and fewer when prices are high, reducing the impact of volatility and removing the pressure to time the market.
details.whyItMatters: Market timing is notoriously difficult even for professionals. Dollar cost averaging removes emotion from investing and ensures consistent participation in market growth over time without stressful entry-point decisions.
takeaways: Invest a fixed dollar amount on a regular schedule regardless of price
You buy more shares when prices drop and fewer when prices rise
This strategy removes the emotional pressure of trying to time markets

faq.question: Is dollar cost averaging better than investing a lump sum?
faq.answer: Historically, lump sum investing beats DCA about two-thirds of the time because markets tend to rise. However, DCA reduces the risk of investing everything at a market peak and is psychologically easier, which helps investors stay committed.

faq.question: How often should you invest when dollar cost averaging?
faq.answer: Monthly is most common and aligns with paychecks. Weekly or biweekly works too but adds minimal benefit over monthly. The key is consistency. Many brokerages offer automatic investment plans that handle the scheduling for you.
